newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Mountain rebel base bows to Cambodian government.
newsitem.headline: Mountain rebel base bows to Cambodian government.

text.p: Nearly 2,000 dissident Khmer Rouge guerrillas formally came over to the Cambodian government on Thursday, the second such major defection in two days.
In a ceremony at this sprawling base on the Thai border, the Khmer Rouge force of 1,907 was represented by 407 fighters who donned new army uniforms.

The group, which is loyal to Ieng Sary, former Khmer Rouge foreign minister, handed over two tanks and 1,115 assorted other weapons at a ceremony presided over by co-Defence Ministers Tea Chamrath and Tea Banh.

"Now it is your duty to defend the country alongside government troops," Tea Chamrath told the former guerrillas at Phnom Malai, one of two major bases held by commanders loyal to Ieng Sary on the northwest border.

An estimated 700 breakaway Khmer Rouge guerrillas, representing a group of 2,500 defectors and 17,000 family members, received royal armed forces uniforms and new weapons at the Pailin base, further south, on Wednesday.

Sok Peap, commander of the Malai-based Khmer Rouge Division 450, said the men were coming over to the government side almost exactly three months after Ieng Sary split with hardliners loyal to rebel leader Pol Pot.
An artillery commander, Suon Sing, said the absent soldiers were at frontline areas to protect the base.
The Cambodian government had urged Ieng Sary to speed up reconciliation after he was pardoned in September.

The Khmer Rouge were included in a 1991 U.N.-brokered peace accord as one of the country's four main warring factions. The guerrillas reneged on the pact and had been fighting the coalition formed after 1993 elections.
More than a million people died during the Khmer Rouge 1975-79 "killing fields" regime.
